chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Hiding the oboe; Joseph Wagner and the Boston Civic Symphony in 1926
summary: He was ashamed to play oboe in Boston dance circles; school conductor Joseph Wagner gave no private lessons, and he played with the Boston Civic Symphony for about a season.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now, in these dances that you went to, did you ever
Holmes (10/9) - 17
bring your oboe and try to sit in or anything?
No! It's not a dance instrument.
No, I understand that.
No, definitely not.
But if your desire was so great, maybe you would try, even on the oboe.

No, no. I was ashamed to let people around Boston know I played oboe. The first thing they wanted to know was, 'What is an oboe?' They was just like I was. I never heard of an oboe until Dr. Holmes gave it to me.
Now, later on you must have studied with a Joseph Wagner in Boston.
Well, he was the conductor of the school symphony. He was the conductor.
I see. So he didn't give you any private tuition.
No. No private tuition.
He gave tuition to the whole band.
The only private tuition I had was with Trogliano(?). That's the one who kept me on the C scale.
Then through Joseph Wagner and playing with the school orchestra, you played in the Boston Civic Symphony Orchestra in 1926.
Yeah, that's right. But I don't remember the conductor's name of that.
Holmes (10/9) - 18
Were you part of that for a long time, then? You must have been going to rehearsals and things with the symphony orchestra. You didn't just sit in there.
Yes, I did.
For just one performance?
No-no-no, I was going to it.
So you attended rehearsals?
